title: Highest temperature in London on August 11?
description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 11 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecasts from major models, including those referenced by Météo-France and European ensembles, indicate a peak temperature near 32°C for Paris on August 11, 2026, driven by persistent high pressure, light southerly flow, and limited cloud cover that favors daytime heating without excessive advection of hotter air masses. eventMetadata.context_description: A strong cold front and associated upper-level trough, which made landfall over the Western Cape earlier in the long weekend, remain the dominant influence on Cape Town’s August 11 temperatures. Post-frontal southwesterly flow, persistent cloud cover, and elevated wind speeds are limiting daytime heating despite moderating maritime air. Ensemble forecasts and South African Weather Service guidance converge on a maximum near the seasonal average of 18 °C, with limited recovery expected; historical analogs for similar August systems rarely exceed 20–21 °C. These conditions underpin the market-implied probabilities favoring 19 °C (57 %) and 20 °C (26.5 %), while lower outcomes reflect residual uncertainty in exact cloud timing and wind strength ahead of final observational verification.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 11 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/zhengzhou/ZHCC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast consensus from meteorological models points to a passing frontal system and monsoon moisture advection bringing persistent cloud cover, northeasterly winds, and precipitation to Zhengzhou on August 11, which limits solar insolation and caps surface heating well below the typical mid-August average of 31–33°C. These conditions favor daily maxima clustered around 25–27°C, with minor differences among leading outcomes driven by uncertainty in exact cloud thickness, rainfall timing, and boundary-layer mixing. High humidity further moderates peaks by enhancing evaporative cooling and reducing net radiative warming, while historical analogs of similar synoptic patterns confirm suppressed highs in this range when overcast skies dominate.
